## Package limes

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes"`

<a id="limes.MaxBiscuitBlocks"></a>

### limes.MaxBiscuitBlocks

```go
const MaxBiscuitBlocks = 32
```

MaxBiscuitBlocks bounds the attenuation blocks a Biscuit may carry. Each block is a revocation id the verifier looks up, and anyone holding a copy can append blocks offline, so an unbounded chain is a lookup per block on every request. Attenuate refuses to go past it, and the verifier refuses a token that has.

<a id="limes.ErrBiscuitAttenuation"></a>

### limes.ErrBiscuitAttenuation

```go
var ErrBiscuitAttenuation error = &familyError{"limes: invalid Biscuit attenuation", ErrInvalidToken}
```

ErrBiscuitAttenuation — an attenuation block the verifier cannot honour: outside the vocabulary, malformed, or widening its parent. Matches ErrInvalidToken: the token is not one this verifier accepts.

<sub>[sealed_form.go](../../sealed_form.go)</sub>
<a id="limes.ErrCopyCountersNotMetered"></a>

### limes.ErrCopyCountersNotMetered

```go
var ErrCopyCountersNotMetered = errors.New("limes: copy limits need a verifier with MeterCopies")
```

ErrCopyCountersNotMetered — a Biscuit sets a copy's own request or budget limit, and the verifier was not told that its Meter counts copies. The limit would go unenforced, so the token is refused instead. The token is not at fault — a verifier with MeterCopies accepts it — so this is the server's configuration, outside ErrInvalidToken: ErrorResponse answers it as an internal error, and it has no Reason.

<a id="limes.Attenuation"></a>

### limes.Attenuation

```go
type Attenuation struct {
	// Ops the token keeps.
	Ops []Op
	// ResourcePrefixes and ResourceURIs the token keeps. Setting either
	// replaces both.
	ResourcePrefixes []string
	ResourceURIs     []string
	// Audience the token keeps.
	Audience []string
	// ExpiresAt, when earlier than the token's, becomes its expiry.
	ExpiresAt time.Time
	// ConfirmationJKT binds the token to a key (dpop.Thumbprint). Only an
	// unbound token can be bound offline: a bound one stays bound to its key,
	// because rebinding needs no key and anyone could do it.
	ConfirmationJKT string
	// Requests and Budget give this copy limits of its own, counted apart
	// from its siblings' and within the capability's: requests made with
	// it, and its spend in the capability's unit, which a block does not
	// carry — so Budget names no UnitCode, and the verifier gives it the
	// capability's. nil sets none; a ceiling of 0 freezes the copy. Each
	// must be within every limit already in force, and an Unlimited one is
	// refused: a copy only narrows.
	Requests *RequestCeiling
	Budget   *BudgetCeiling
}
```

Attenuation is one offline narrowing. Empty fields leave that dimension as it is; set ones replace it and must be within what the token already allows, or the verifier refuses the whole token.

<a id="limes.Attenuation.Validate"></a>

#### limes.Attenuation.Validate

```go
func (a Attenuation) Validate() error
```

Validate refuses an attenuation no block can carry: a binding that is no thumbprint, or a copy limit that is not a bound. The verifier refuses such a block whatever form carried it.

<a id="limes.TokenForm"></a>

### limes.TokenForm

```go
type TokenForm interface {
	// Seal builds a token around the JWT sign returns for the root key the
	// form chose, whose private half signs the token's first block and is
	// then dropped.
	Seal(ctx context.Context, sign func(ctx context.Context, root ed25519.PublicKey) (string, error)) (string, error)

	// Open splits token into the JWT it seals and unseal, which, once the
	// caller has verified that JWT and hands it the root key the JWT names,
	// verifies the rest of token under it and returns what it read. Nothing
	// of token is to be trusted before unseal returns.
	Open(token string) (sealed string, unseal func(root ed25519.PublicKey) (Unsealed, error), err error)
}
```

TokenForm is a form of capability token that seals a JWT this issuer signed inside a token its holder can narrow offline: the Biscuit form (IssuerConfig.Biscuit, BiscuitConfig.Form). The form reads and writes its encoding and verifies its signatures; the core keeps what a narrowing may do. Every block a form hands back is checked as the holder's input (Attenuation, Narrows), whatever form decoded it.

A form's error refuses the token as ErrBiscuitAttenuation when it wraps that sentinel, and as ErrInvalidToken otherwise. The form need not wrap either: an error that does keeps its text, one that does not gets the family's prefixed, and the family is named once either way.

<a id="limes.Unsealed"></a>

### limes.Unsealed

```go
type Unsealed struct {
	// Blocks are the token's attenuations, in the order they were appended.
	Blocks []Attenuation
	// RevocationIDs are the token's revocation ids: its first block's, then
	// one for each of Blocks.
	RevocationIDs [][]byte
}
```

Unsealed is what a TokenForm read of a token past its sealed JWT, its signature chain verified.

<a id="biscuit"></a><a id="package-biscuit"></a>

## Package biscuit

`import "github.com/oleg-tkachuk/limes/biscuit"`

Package biscuit is the Biscuit form of a limes capability token: a Biscuit v3 whose authority block seals the JWT an issuer signed, and whose attenuation blocks its holder appends offline (Attenuate). Give Form to limes.IssuerConfig.Biscuit and limes.BiscuitConfig.Form. A module of its own, so that a consumer of JWT capabilities alone resolves neither biscuit-go nor protobuf (docs/adr/0008-biscuit-module.md).

<a id="biscuit.Attenuate"></a>

### biscuit.Attenuate

```go
func Attenuate(token string, a limes.Attenuation) (string, error)
```

Attenuate appends a block that narrows token. It needs no key and no network; the result is a new token, and the input still works as before.
